The (Ga,Mn)As nanowire shells have a wurtzite crystal structure.
The nanowires were grown using molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) on the {1100} side facets of wurtzite (Ga,In)As nanowires.
The core is composed of (Ga,In)As, the inner shell is composed of (Ga,Al)As, and the outer shell is composed of (Ga,Mn)As and low-temperature GaAs.
The average surface density of the nanowires is estimated to be 109 cm-2.
The typical diameter of the nanowires increases from about 70 nm at the bottom part to a maximum of 200 nm at the 3/5 of their height.
The thickness of the (Ga,Mn)As/LT-GaAs shells changes from 5 nm at the bottom part to 45-50 nm in the widest parts directly exposed to the element fluxes.
The composition of the NW constituents derived from EDS analysis is: 8-10% In in the core, 35%-40% Al in the inner shell, and 5% Mn in the (Ga,Mn)As shell.
The Mn distribution in the (Ga,Mn)As shell is homogenous.
The average density of stacking faults (SFs) is in the range 20-60 SF/micrometer of the NW length.
The main result is the direct observation of a spontaneous magnetic moment, m, manifested as a non-zero magnetic signal which appears below about 25 K every time the NWs are cooled.
The existence of such a spontaneously appearing magnetic moment is the hallmark of the presence of a long-range magnetic order in the investigated material.
The NWs were studied using scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) and energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS).
The NWs were also studied using room-temperature Raman scattering (RS) measurements.
The NWs were grown on GaAs(111)B substrates using Au catalyst.
The NWs were annealed at 180°C for 4 hours at ambient pressure.
The NWs were also annealed at 450°C for 30 minutes inside the MBE chamber.
